description: Only exact claim and complete 2-paper group decisions from 24 October 2026 review. Individual source and claim records must not be banned.

decisions.reason: Both papers re-pose the same question (emissions versus climate as drivers of European air quality at the 2050 horizon) with CMIP6/SSP scenarios. They show how the question is being re-projected; they are not evidence of outcomes and carry low evidential weight.
The claim concerns EU gas import dependence and the Southern Gas Corridor; neither paper concerns energy, gas or supply security. The match rests on “predict”, “current” and “estimates”.
Both papers concern renewable deployment inside the EU only; neither measures, explains or reframes renewable electricity in North Africa or its exchange with Europe.
The claim concerns the feasibility of a Europe-wide CO₂ pipeline network for CCS; neither paper addresses CCS, CO₂ infrastructure or decarbonisation pathways.
Paper A is unrelated to the FOCUS role-space claim; Paper B is at most tangential and is recorded separately as a pair-level UNCERTAIN pending a full-text check.
Paper A is unrelated to the claim’s warning about EU decline, US dependence and strategic unity. Paper B is relevant but weak and is kept at pair level.
Paper B is unrelated to the EU’s evolution as a military power. Paper A is relevant but weak (a non-peer-reviewed preprint) and is kept at pair level.
Paper A is unrelated to the ozone-exposure projection. Paper B is relevant explanatory evidence and is kept at pair level.
The claim concerns climate-driven changes in ozone-related mortality and morbidity; neither paper deals with ozone, air pollution or health. The match rests on the words “baseline” and “impact”.
Paper A is unrelated to mosquito climatic suitability. Paper B is relevant and is kept at pair level.
Paper B is unrelated to the EU-level stock-versus-increment question. Paper A is relevant and is kept at pair level.
The claim concerns deregulation of Finland–Russia rail transport; neither paper concerns rail, transport markets or Finland–Russia relations.
The claim concerns backcasting scenarios for a low-emission Finland in 2050; neither paper concerns Finland, emissions, energy or futures methods.
The claim concerns UK obesity projections and policy choices; both papers matched only on the word “prediction”.
Neither paper measures, explains or re-projects obesity prevalence or obesity-related costs in Ireland; the overlap is limited to terms such as “direct costs”.
The claim concerns scenarios for the supply of NHS nurses in England; neither paper concerns nursing, workforce planning or the NHS. The match rests on the words “different” and “important”.

The claim concerns health impacts of landfills and incinerators under operating scenarios to 2050; both papers are technical studies of facility processes and say nothing about exposure, health or the facility trajectories assumed.
The claim concerns immigration and integration scenarios for Europe to 2050; neither publication addresses migration, integration or demography. The match rests on “integration” and “European”.
The claim concerns superconducting technologies and their environmental role; the papers matched only on “want” and “stabilize”.
Both papers share only the Delphi method with the original study; neither concerns farmers’ markets, local food systems or the social economy.
